text:
Mathew Barzal is four games into his return from injury, and the Islanders are bringing him back slowly. He is playing 16 minutes a night, under his normal load, and Pete DeBoer told NHL.com's Stefen Rosner: "We've managed his minutes. I think he's ready for more." The early signs say he should get it. In those four games he has three assists, and the Islanders have taken 70% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice (expected goals measure the quality of chances). Four games is a tiny sample, but that is what he does.

Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among all forwards in wins above replacement last season, 97th percentile for driving play. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why: he carries the puck in on 66% of his entries and leaves his own zone with possession 74% of the time. He is skating with Victor Eklund, a rookie who grew up idolizing him, and Brayden Schenn. Watch the minutes. When they climb, the points usually follow.
